transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm... well, my name is Mark. I'm a composer. I'm here because... I guess I've been having some trouble at work for a while now. Almost two years, actually. Ever since a big commission I had. 

It's just... I know that a few people in the ensemble have been trying to undermine me. Quietly, you know? Changing the schedule around, picking certain seats during rehearsals... making little comments. They show me emails and notes that supposedly explain it all away, but... I know what they're doing. I just can't shake it.
Mark, beyond these feelings about your colleagues, have you ever heard or seen things that others around you seem unable to perceive?
No. I don't... I don't hear things or see things that aren't there. It's nothing like that. I just... I see what they're doing. The things that are actually happening. That's all.
Mark, do you feel this same sense of distrust and suspicion toward your friends or family members as you do toward your colleagues?

No. Not at all. It's just... that specific group. 

Outside of this issue with the ensemble, everything else is fine. I still meet my deadlines, I keep up with my composing... I run most mornings. And things at home with my wife are basically steady. So... no. It's just them.
Do you feel that these colleagues are working together as part of a larger, organized group or plot to ruin your career?
No... I wouldn't say that. It's not some... big conspiracy or anything like that. Just... just those few individuals in the ensemble. That's all.
Mark, what specific reason do you believe these colleagues have for wanting to undermine you?
I don't... I don't really know why. I just know they're doing it. Maybe they're jealous, or they just don't like me... but I don't know for sure. I just see what they're doing.
Mark, do you find yourself frequently questioning the loyalty or trustworthiness of people you meet in other areas of your life, such as your neighbors or people you encounter while running?
No. I told you, it's just the ensemble. My neighbors are... fine. I don't really talk to people when I run. So, no.
Mark, when you are composing or talking to others, do you ever feel like your thoughts become muddled, or that you have difficulty keeping your train of thought on track?
No. My thoughts are fine. I don't have trouble thinking or... or talking. It's just normal.

Mark, have you generally been a person who is suspicious of others throughout your life, or is this specific feeling about your colleagues something that only started when these problems at work began?
No, I haven't always been like that. It really just started after I won the commission. When I got invited to conduct the premiere... that was about a year and nine months ago. So, just since then.
Mark, do you believe these colleagues are doing things that are specifically intended to cause you physical or professional harm?

Well... professional harm, yes. I mean, that's why I'm here. For almost two years now, I've just had this... this certainty. After the commission, a few people in the ensemble started doing things. Just... little things. Schedule changes, where they sit, little comments during rehearsals. It's to quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain why they did it... I know what they're doing.
Mark, have you felt unusually energetic, or have you noticed that you require significantly less sleep than usual since this started?
No. I mean... my sleep is fine. I haven't noticed needing less of it, or feeling extra energetic. Just the usual amount, I guess.
Mark, do you feel that these colleagues monitor your activities or track your movements outside of the rehearsals?

No, not really. I mean... I haven't noticed them following me or anything like that. It's mostly just... at work. During rehearsals and things related to the music. I don't think they care what I do on my own time.
